expectations.text: Plan explores what causes the addition_position_preserved failure — not just where to add a fix but why it fails
expectations.evidence: Plan Context section explains the causal chain: '1. V1Extractor.build_word_sequence() counts the placeholder's value as an ADDITION token. 2. The migration itself suppresses the placeholder (because IGNORE means skip), so V2 XML does not contain the placeholder as an addition. 3. PositionPreservedAxiom finds the V1 addition has no matching V2 position and raises a violation — even though migration was correct.' It also explains WHY: 'After the refactor in cb77627, the method was changed to always emit text_type=ChangeType.ADDITION (correct for non-IGNORE cases), but the IGNORE suppression was not added.'

suggestions.reason: Assertion 6 ('explores what causes the failure') is satisfied by the plan's Context section. However, the assertion could be tightened to require that the exploration section names the specific commit or code path responsible — plans that just describe the symptom without the mechanism would also pass a weaker version of this check. This eval's assertion is actually fairly strong; noting it is above-average quality.

No assertion checks that Task 2 (walk() integration test) is present. A plan that only has Task 1 (unit test) and Task 3 (CLI regression) would pass all current assertions but would miss the integration-level coverage. An assertion like 'plan includes integration tests verifying the fix through the walk() call chain' would be discriminating.

eval_feedback.overall: All 8 assertions pass. This eval is the most discriminating in the iteration — assertion 6 requires genuine causal analysis, not just symptom description. The CLI regression command check (assertion 5) is well-targeted. One gap: no assertion for integration-level walk() coverage.
